Subject: Request: pilot uptime adjustment + latency guardrails for AegisMed (deal desk approval)

Hi team,

Quick summary: AegisMed (pilot, potential Dedicated commitment) is asking for a non-standard SLO for the initial 3-month pilot: reduce uptime target from 99.95% to 99.8% and soften the immediate service-credit remedy (they'll accept a graded makeup plan rather than a straight credit). They are asking for a 30% pilot discount on committed capacity if we grant the SLO adjustment.

Why this matters: AegisMed is a high-touch prospect in the payer/health segment — pilot could convert to Dedicated in Q4 with multi-region requirements. The risk is slightly higher operational exposure; we would want enforceable guardrails (latency p95 <= 220ms for production traffic tiers, weekly health checks, and a remediation milestone plan with staged credits capped at 12% of monthly commit).

What I'm asking for: executive signoff (deal desk + finance + product ops alignment) to offer the pilot package below: 
- Temporary uptime target: 99.8% for initial 90 days (then roll back to standard 99.95% for production)
- Remedy: staged makeup plan (week 1: operational remediation / no credit; weeks 2-4: incremental credits 2%/4%/6% capped at 12%)
- Discount: 30% off monthly Dedicated pilot rate (applies only to committed pilot capacity)
- Required guardrails: weekly incident review, latency p95 <=220ms, monthly performance report to customer

Attachments: SLO-Adjustment-Map_AegisMed.pdf (proposal), cost-impact-model.xlsx (finance calc), AegisMed-MSA-terms_redline.docx (legal redlines).

Can you confirm if we can approve this commercially and who needs to be looped for final signoff? I can prepare a one-page exec note for Marissa to present.

Thanks,
Stephanie
